policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere שָׁפְכוּ (3mp) and ketiv שפכה (3fs) differ only in verbal agreement with the plural/dual subject יָדֵינוּ; a feminine singular verb with a dual subject is ordinary Hebrew concord. ASV 'Our hands have not shed this blood' renders the same clause either way, since English supplies plural agreement with 'hands' regardless, and there is no ASV note at this word. Nothing in the English distinguishes the two, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
